```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

source("00_helpers.R")

required_packages <- c(
  "dplyr", "tidyr", "stringr", "stringi", "lubridate", "forcats", "tibble",
  "ggplot2", "scales", "patchwork", "ggrepel",
  "knitr", "kableExtra",
  "fixest",        # fixed-effects estimation
  "sandwich",      # HAC standard errors
  "lmtest",        # coefficient tests
  "strucchange",   # structural break detection
  "MASS",          # negative binomial
  "broom",         # tidy model output
  "zoo"            # rolling means
)
load_packages(required_packages)
select <- dplyr::select

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE, scipen = 999)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "C"))   # English month labels

theme_pub <- theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle    = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.title     = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text        = element_text(color = "black")
  )
theme_set(theme_pub)

# Table with a short caption (set in the chunk) and the notes below it
kbl_note <- function(df, note, col.names = NA, digits = getOption("digits"), ...) {
  kable(df, col.names = col.names, digits = digits, ...) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) |>
    footnote(general = note, general_title = "Note:", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE,
             threeparttable = TRUE)
}
fmt1 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)
fmt2 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
fmt3 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
fmt4 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 4)
fmtN <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",")
fmtP <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))
```

```{r}
#| label: analysis
#| include: false

# ==========================================================================
# DATA — extended corpus from the merged Determ database (01_extract_corpus.R)
# All estimates are computed here once; later chunks only display them, and
# every number quoted in the text comes from the `kn` list at the end.
# ==========================================================================

if (!file.exists(path_raw_corpus_extended)) {
  stop("Corpus not found at ", path_raw_corpus_extended, ". Run R/01_extract_corpus.R first.")
}

CHATGPT_DATE <- as.Date(CONFIG$paper1_events$treatment)
PLACEBO_DATE <- as.Date(CONFIG$paper1_events$placebo)
events_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(date = CHATGPT_DATE, label = "ChatGPT"),
  tibble(date  = as.Date(sapply(CONFIG$paper1_events$secondary, `[[`, "date")),
         label = sapply(CONFIG$paper1_events$secondary, `[[`, "label"))
)

corpus_data <- readRDS(path_raw_corpus_extended) |>
  mutate(
    DATE       = as.Date(DATE),
    year       = year(DATE),
    year_month = floor_date(DATE, "month"),
    word_count = stri_count_regex(FULL_TEXT, "\\S+")
  ) |>
  arrange(DATE)

frame_dictionaries <- lapply(CONFIG$frames, `[[`, "keywords")
all_frames <- names(frame_dictionaries)
frame_cols <- paste0("frame_", all_frames)
for (f in all_frames) {
  corpus_data[[paste0("frame_", f)]] <- stri_detect_regex(
    corpus_data$.text_lower, paste(frame_dictionaries[[f]], collapse = "|"))
}

corpus_data <- bind_cols(corpus_data, classify_outlets(corpus_data$FROM, corpus_data$SOURCE_TYPE)) |>
  mutate(
    outlet_type  = case_when(!is.na(outlet_type) ~ outlet_type,
                             SOURCE_TYPE == "web" ~ "Other web",
                             TRUE ~ "Non-web"),
    outlet_type  = factor(outlet_type, levels = c("Tabloid", "Quality", "Regional", "Public",
                                                  "Tech", "Business", "Other web", "Non-web")),
    threat       = frame_JOB_LOSS | frame_FEAR_RESISTANCE | frame_INEQUALITY,
    opportunity  = frame_JOB_CREATION | frame_PRODUCTIVITY | frame_TRANSFORMATION,
    post_chatgpt = as.integer(DATE >= CHATGPT_DATE),
    month_idx    = (year(year_month) - year(min(year_month))) * 12 +
                   month(year_month) - month(min(year_month)),
    rel_month    = interval(CHATGPT_DATE, year_month) %/% months(1)
  )
T_STAR <- unique(corpus_data$month_idx[corpus_data$year_month == CHATGPT_DATE])
hac <- function(m) coeftest(m, vcov = vcovHAC(m))

# --- Monthly volume ----------------------------------------------------------
monthly <- corpus_data |>
  count(year_month, month_idx) |>
  mutate(post = as.integer(year_month >= CHATGPT_DATE), t = month_idx,
         moy = factor(month(year_month)))

its_model  <- lm(n ~ t + post + I((t - T_STAR) * post), data = monthly)
its_robust <- hac(its_model)
monthly$fitted <- predict(its_model)

vol_m1 <- glm(n ~ post,           data = monthly, family = quasipoisson())
vol_m2 <- glm(n ~ post + t,       data = monthly, family = quasipoisson())
vol_m3 <- glm(n ~ post + t + moy, data = monthly, family = quasipoisson())
outlet_month_panel <- corpus_data |>
  count(FROM, year_month) |>
  mutate(post = as.integer(year_month >= CHATGPT_DATE), moy = factor(month(year_month)))
vol_m4 <- fixest::feglm(n ~ post | FROM + moy, data = outlet_month_panel,
                        family = poisson, cluster = "FROM")
vol_nb <- MASS::glm.nb(n ~ post + t, data = monthly)

# --- Structural breaks -------------------------------------------------------
fs_test   <- Fstats(n ~ t, data = monthly, from = 0.15)
bp_all    <- breakpoints(n ~ t, data = monthly, h = 0.15)
bp_ci     <- confint(bp_all)$confint
fs_log    <- Fstats(log(n) ~ t, data = monthly, from = 0.15)
cusum_test <- efp(n ~ t, data = monthly, type = "OLS-CUSUM")
ym_lab <- function(i) format(monthly$year_month[i], "%b %Y")

# --- Frame panel ---------------------------------------------------------------
frame_monthly <- corpus_data |>
  group_by(year_month, month_idx, rel_month) |>
  summarise(n_total = n(), across(all_of(frame_cols), ~ sum(.x)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(frame_cols), names_to = "frame", values_to = "count") |>
  mutate(frame = str_remove(frame, "frame_"), pct = 100 * count / n_total,
         post = as.integer(year_month >= CHATGPT_DATE), t = month_idx)

# Event study: three-month event-time bins, reference = Sep-Nov 2022
es_bin <- function(k) floor(k / 3)
es_results <- bind_rows(lapply(all_frames, function(f) {
  d  <- filter(frame_monthly, frame == f) |>
    mutate(q = relevel(factor(es_bin(rel_month)), ref = "-1"))
  ct <- hac(lm(pct ~ q, data = d))
  tibble(frame = f, term = rownames(ct), estimate = ct[, 1], se = ct[, 2], p = ct[, 4]) |>
    filter(str_detect(term, "^q")) |>
    mutate(bin = as.integer(str_remove(term, "q")),
           bin_start = CHATGPT_DATE %m+% months(3 * bin),
           conf.low = estimate - 1.96 * se, conf.high = estimate + 1.96 * se)
}))

# Pre-trend tests on the pre-launch months
pre_bins <- function(k) cut(k, breaks = c(-24, seq(-20, -2, by = 3)), right = TRUE)
pretrend_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(all_frames, function(f) {
  d <- filter(frame_monthly, frame == f, rel_month <= -2)
  d$bin <- relevel(factor(pre_bins(d$rel_month)), ref = "(-5,-2]")
  a <- anova(lm(pct ~ t, d), lm(pct ~ bin + t, d))
  s <- summary(lm(pct ~ t, d))$coefficients
  tibble(Frame = f, F_stat = a$F[2], F_p = a$`Pr(>F)`[2], slope = s["t", 1], slope_p = s["t", 4])
}))

# Average post-launch effects (post + linear trend, HAC)
ate_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(all_frames, function(f) {
  d <- filter(frame_monthly, frame == f)
  r <- hac(lm(pct ~ post + t, data = d))
  tibble(Frame = f, pre = mean(d$pct[d$post == 0]), post_mean = mean(d$pct[d$post == 1]),
         ate = r["post", 1], se = r["post", 2], p = r["post", 4])
})) |> arrange(desc(abs(ate)))

# Composite indices
composite_monthly <- corpus_data |>
  group_by(year_month, month_idx) |>
  summarise(n = n(), threat = 100 * mean(threat), opportunity = 100 * mean(opportunity),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(gap = threat - opportunity, post = as.integer(year_month >= CHATGPT_DATE),
         t = month_idx)
comp_fit <- lapply(c(threat = "threat", opportunity = "opportunity", gap = "gap"),
                   function(y) hac(lm(reformulate(c("post", "t"), y), data = composite_monthly)))

# Persistence: post-launch slopes
decay_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(c(all_frames, "threat", "opportunity", "gap"), function(f) {
  d <- if (f %in% all_frames) filter(frame_monthly, frame == f, post == 1) |> mutate(y = pct)
       else filter(composite_monthly, post == 1) |> mutate(y = .data[[f]])
  d$ms <- d$t - T_STAR
  r <- hac(lm(y ~ ms, data = d))
  tibble(Series = f, level0 = r[1, 1], slope = r[2, 1], se = r[2, 2], p = r[2, 4])
}))

# --- Platforms --------------------------------------------------------------------
all_months <- distinct(monthly, year_month, month_idx)
platform_its <- bind_rows(lapply(sort(unique(corpus_data$SOURCE_TYPE)), function(p) {
  d <- corpus_data |> filter(SOURCE_TYPE == p) |> count(year_month, month_idx) |>
    right_join(all_months, by = c("year_month", "month_idx")) |>
    mutate(n = coalesce(n, 0L), post = as.integer(year_month >= CHATGPT_DATE), t = month_idx)
  pre_items <- sum(d$n[d$post == 0])
  out <- tibble(Platform = p, total = sum(d$n), pre_items = pre_items,
                pre_mo = mean(d$n[d$post == 0]), post_mo = mean(d$n[d$post == 1]),
                level = NA_real_, level_p = NA_real_, slope = NA_real_, slope_p = NA_real_)
  if (pre_items >= 30) {
    r <- hac(lm(n ~ t + post + I((t - T_STAR) * post), data = d))
    out$level <- r["post", 1]; out$level_p <- r["post", 4]
    out$slope <- r[4, 1];      out$slope_p <- r[4, 4]
  }
  out
})) |> arrange(desc(total))

# --- Tabloid vs quality DiD (web items, named outlets) -------------------------------
did_data <- corpus_data |>
  filter(outlet_type %in% c("Tabloid", "Quality")) |>
  mutate(threat_i = as.integer(threat), tabloid = as.integer(outlet_type == "Tabloid"),
         post_tab = post_chatgpt * tabloid)
did_hetero <- feols(threat_i ~ post_tab + tabloid | year_month, did_data, vcov = "hetero")
did_2way   <- feols(threat_i ~ post_tab + tabloid | year_month, did_data,
                    cluster = c("outlet", "year_month"))
did_dm     <- demean(cbind(y = did_data$threat_i, post_tab = did_data$post_tab,
                           tabloid = did_data$tabloid), did_data$year_month)
did_wild   <- wild_cluster_p(did_dm[, "y"], did_dm[, c("post_tab", "tabloid")],
                             did_data$outlet, "post_tab", B = 9999, weights = "webb")
did_n1 <- feols(threat_i ~ post_tab + tabloid | year_month,
                did_data |> mutate(tabloid = as.integer(tabloid == 1 | outlet == "N1 Hrvatska"),
                                   post_tab = post_chatgpt * tabloid),
                cluster = c("outlet", "year_month"))
did_means <- did_data |> group_by(outlet_type, post_chatgpt) |>
  summarise(threat = 100 * mean(threat_i), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
dm_ <- function(ty, p) did_means$threat[did_means$outlet_type == ty & did_means$post_chatgpt == p]

# Threat and opportunity by outlet type
type_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(levels(corpus_data$outlet_type), function(ty) {
  d <- corpus_data |> filter(outlet_type == ty) |>
    group_by(year_month, month_idx) |>
    summarise(n = n(), threat = 100 * mean(threat), opp = 100 * mean(opportunity), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(post = as.integer(year_month >= CHATGPT_DATE), t = month_idx)
  x_ <- corpus_data |> filter(outlet_type == ty)
  rt <- hac(lm(threat ~ post + t, d)); ro <- hac(lm(opp ~ post + t, d))
  tibble(Type = ty, items = nrow(x_),
         thr_pre = 100 * mean(x_$threat[x_$post_chatgpt == 0]),
         thr_post = 100 * mean(x_$threat[x_$post_chatgpt == 1]),
         thr_ate = rt["post", 1], thr_p = rt["post", 4],
         opp_pre = 100 * mean(x_$opportunity[x_$post_chatgpt == 0]),
         opp_post = 100 * mean(x_$opportunity[x_$post_chatgpt == 1]),
         opp_ate = ro["post", 1], opp_p = ro["post", 4])
}))

# --- Mechanisms ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (a) Near-duplicates across outlets: title-token Jaccard >= 0.7 within +-3 days.
#     Candidate pairs are blocked on each title's two rarest tokens.
.tok <- corpus_data |>
  mutate(id = row_number()) |>
  filter(!is.na(TITLE)) |>
  transmute(id, DATE, FROM, tok = stri_extract_all_regex(stri_trans_tolower(TITLE), "\\p{L}{4,}")) |>
  tidyr::unnest(tok) |>
  distinct(id, tok, .keep_all = TRUE)
.ntok <- count(.tok, id, name = "n_tok") |> filter(n_tok >= 3)
.tok  <- semi_join(.tok, .ntok, by = "id")
.keys <- .tok |> add_count(tok, name = "df") |> arrange(id, df, tok) |>
  group_by(id) |> slice_head(n = 2) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(lo = DATE - 3, hi = DATE + 3)
.cand <- inner_join(select(.keys, id, tok, FROM, lo, hi),
                    select(.keys, id2 = id, tok, FROM2 = FROM, DATE2 = DATE),
                    by = join_by(tok, between(y$DATE2, x$lo, x$hi))) |>
  filter(id < id2, FROM != FROM2) |>
  distinct(id, id2)
.inter <- .cand |>
  inner_join(select(.tok, id, tok), by = "id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  semi_join(select(.tok, id2 = id, tok), by = c("id2", "tok")) |>
  count(id, id2, name = "inter") |>
  left_join(.ntok, by = "id") |>
  left_join(rename(.ntok, id2 = id, n_tok2 = n_tok), by = "id2") |>
  mutate(jac = inter / (n_tok + n_tok2 - inter)) |>
  filter(jac >= 0.7)
.dup_ids <- unique(c(.inter$id, .inter$id2))
wire_tbl <- corpus_data |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), near_dup = id %in% .dup_ids) |>
  filter(id %in% .ntok$id) |>
  mutate(Period = ifelse(post_chatgpt == 1, "Post-launch", "Pre-launch")) |>
  group_by(Period) |>
  summarise(items = n(), dups = sum(near_dup), share = 100 * mean(near_dup),
            threat_dup = 100 * mean(threat[near_dup]), threat_nodup = 100 * mean(threat[!near_dup]),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(Period))

# (b) Reader engagement: interactions on web items
eng_data <- corpus_data |> filter(SOURCE_TYPE == "web", !is.na(INTERACTIONS))
eng_all  <- feols(log1p(INTERACTIONS) ~ threat + opportunity | FROM + year_month,
                  eng_data, cluster = "FROM")
eng_pos  <- feols(log(INTERACTIONS) ~ threat + opportunity | FROM + year_month,
                  filter(eng_data, INTERACTIONS > 0), cluster = "FROM")

# --- Robustness: threat composite, post + trend, HAC ------------------------------------
threat_ate <- function(df, var = "threat") {
  m <- df |> group_by(year_month, month_idx) |>
    summarise(y = 100 * mean(.data[[var]]), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(post = as.integer(year_month >= CHATGPT_DATE), t = month_idx)
  r <- hac(lm(y ~ post + t, data = m))
  c(est = r["post", 1], se = r["post", 2], p = r["post", 4])
}
windows <- c(6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36)
window_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(windows, function(w) {
  r <- threat_ate(filter(corpus_data, DATE >= CHATGPT_DATE %m-% months(w),
                         DATE <  CHATGPT_DATE %m+% months(w)))
  tibble(Window = paste0("±", w, " months"), est = r[1], se = r[2], p = r[3])
}))
placebo_data  <- monthly |> filter(year_month < CHATGPT_DATE) |>
  mutate(placebo_post = as.integer(year_month >= PLACEBO_DATE))
placebo_fit   <- hac(lm(n ~ placebo_post + t, data = placebo_data))
tabloid_names <- CONFIG$paper1_outlets$outlets |> Filter(f = function(o) o$type == "Tabloid") |>
  sapply(`[[`, "name")
alt_fear <- corpus_data |> mutate(threat_nofear = frame_JOB_LOSS | frame_INEQUALITY)

rb <- list(
  c("Full sample (reference)", threat_ate(corpus_data)),
  c("Web items only",          threat_ate(filter(corpus_data, SOURCE_TYPE == "web"))),
  c("Excluding January 2023",  threat_ate(filter(corpus_data, year_month != as.Date("2023-01-01")))),
  c("Threat without fear/resistance", threat_ate(alt_fear, "threat_nofear"))
)
for (o in tabloid_names)
  rb[[length(rb) + 1]] <- c(paste("Excluding", o), threat_ate(filter(corpus_data, is.na(outlet) | outlet != o)))
robust_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(rb, function(r) tibble(Specification = r[1], est = as.numeric(r[2]),
                                                      se = as.numeric(r[3]), p = as.numeric(r[4]))))

# LPM with outlet FE, trend and month-of-year FE (year-month FE would absorb `post`)
lpm_fit <- feols(as.integer(threat) ~ post_chatgpt + month_idx | FROM + moy,
                 corpus_data |> mutate(moy = month(year_month)), cluster = "FROM")

# --- Anticipation -------------------------------------------------------------------------
.pre <- corpus_data$DATE < as.Date("2022-11-30")
pre_chatgpt <- sum(.pre & stri_detect_regex(corpus_data$.text_lower, "chat.?gpt"))
pre_gpt     <- sum(.pre & stri_detect_regex(corpus_data$.text_lower, "openai|open ai|\\bgpt\\b|gpt.?[34]"))

# --- Cross-platform duplicates -----------------------------------------------------------
.norm <- function(x) stri_trim(stri_replace_all_regex(stri_trans_tolower(x), "[^\\p{L}\\p{N} ]+", " "))
.fbw <- inner_join(
  corpus_data |> filter(SOURCE_TYPE == "facebook") |> transmute(k = .norm(TITLE), DF = DATE, id_f = row_number()),
  corpus_data |> filter(SOURCE_TYPE == "web") |> transmute(k = .norm(TITLE), DW = DATE),
  by = "k", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(abs(as.numeric(DF - DW)) <= 2, nchar(k) > 25)

# --- Key numbers for the text ---------------------------------------------------------------
es_ <- function(f, bins) mean(es_results$estimate[es_results$frame == f & es_results$bin %in% bins])
late_bins  <- 8:max(es_results$bin)          # December 2024 onward
early_bins <- 0:1                            # first six months
cy <- composite_monthly |> mutate(y = year(year_month)) |> group_by(y) |>
  summarise(threat = mean(threat), opportunity = mean(opportunity), .groups = "drop")
w24 <- window_tbl[window_tbl$Window == "±24 months", ]
w18 <- window_tbl[window_tbl$Window == "±18 months", ]
ate_ <- function(f, col) ate_tbl[[col]][ate_tbl$Frame == f]
forum_tab <- table(corpus_data$FROM[corpus_data$SOURCE_TYPE == "forum"])
bp_dates  <- ym_lab(bp_all$breakpoints)

kn <- list(
  N              = fmtN(nrow(corpus_data)),
  start          = format(min(corpus_data$DATE), "%B %Y"),
  end            = format(max(corpus_data$DATE), "%B %Y"),
  n_pre_months   = sum(monthly$post == 0),
  n_post_months  = sum(monthly$post == 1),
  pre_mean       = fmtN(mean(monthly$n[monthly$post == 0])),
  post_mean      = fmtN(mean(monthly$n[monthly$post == 1])),
  ratio          = fmt1(mean(monthly$n[monthly$post == 1]) / mean(monthly$n[monthly$post == 0])),
  last_year      = max(year(monthly$year_month)),
  last_year_mean = fmtN(mean(monthly$n[year(monthly$year_month) == max(year(monthly$year_month))])),
  first_year_mean = fmtN(mean(monthly$n[year(monthly$year_month) == 2021])),
  its_level      = fmt1(its_robust["post", 1]),
  its_level_p    = fmt2(its_robust["post", 4]),
  its_slope      = fmt1(its_robust[4, 1]),
  its_slope_se   = fmt1(its_robust[4, 2]),
  its_pretrend   = fmt1(its_robust["t", 1]),
  irr_raw        = fmt2(exp(coef(vol_m1)["post"])),
  irr_trend      = fmt2(exp(coef(vol_m2)["post"])),
  irr_trend_p    = fmt2(summary(vol_m2)$coefficients["post", 4]),
  irr_outlet     = fmt2(exp(coef(vol_m4)["post"])),
  supf           = fmt1(max(fs_test$Fstats)),
  supf_date      = ym_lab(fs_test$breakpoint),
  supf_log_date  = ym_lab(fs_log$breakpoint),
  bp1            = bp_dates[1],
  bp1_lo         = ym_lab(bp_ci[1, 1]), bp1_hi = ym_lab(bp_ci[1, 3]),
  bp2            = if (length(bp_dates) > 1) bp_dates[2] else NA,
  bp2_lo         = if (nrow(bp_ci) > 1) ym_lab(bp_ci[2, 1]) else NA,
  bp2_hi         = if (nrow(bp_ci) > 1) ym_lab(bp_ci[2, 3]) else NA,
  placebo        = fmt1(placebo_fit["placebo_post", 1]),
  placebo_p      = fmt2(placebo_fit["placebo_post", 4]),
  threat_pre     = fmt1(mean(composite_monthly$threat[composite_monthly$post == 0])),
  threat_post    = fmt1(mean(composite_monthly$threat[composite_monthly$post == 1])),
  opp_pre        = fmt1(mean(composite_monthly$opportunity[composite_monthly$post == 0])),
  opp_post       = fmt1(mean(composite_monthly$opportunity[composite_monthly$post == 1])),
  gap_pre        = fmt1(mean(composite_monthly$gap[composite_monthly$post == 0])),
  gap_post       = fmt1(mean(composite_monthly$gap[composite_monthly$post == 1])),
  threat_last    = fmt1(cy$threat[cy$y == max(cy$y)]),
  threat_ate     = fmt1(comp_fit$threat["post", 1]),  threat_ate_p = fmt2(comp_fit$threat["post", 4]),
  opp_ate        = fmt1(comp_fit$opportunity["post", 1]), opp_ate_p = fmt2(comp_fit$opportunity["post", 4]),
  gap_ate        = fmt1(comp_fit$gap["post", 1]),     gap_ate_p = fmt2(comp_fit$gap["post", 4]),
  w24            = fmt1(w24$est), w24_p = fmt2(w24$p),
  w18            = fmt1(w18$est), w18_p = fmt2(w18$p),
  fear_early     = fmt1(es_("FEAR_RESISTANCE", early_bins)),
  fear_late      = fmt1(es_("FEAR_RESISTANCE", late_bins)),
  skills_ate     = fmt1(ate_("SKILLS", "ate")), skills_p = fmtP(ate_("SKILLS", "p")),
  skills_late    = fmt1(es_("SKILLS", late_bins)),
  reg_peak       = fmt1(max(es_results$estimate[es_results$frame == "REGULATION"])),
  reg_peak_date  = format(es_results$bin_start[es_results$frame == "REGULATION"][
                     which.max(es_results$estimate[es_results$frame == "REGULATION"])], "%B %Y"),
  prod_early     = fmt1(es_("PRODUCTIVITY", early_bins)),
  prod_late      = fmt1(es_("PRODUCTIVITY", late_bins)),
  did_coef       = fmt1(100 * coef(did_2way)["post_tab"]),
  did_p          = fmt3(pvalue(did_2way)["post_tab"]),
  did_p_wild     = fmt3(did_wild$p),
  did_G          = did_wild$G,
  did_n1         = fmt1(100 * coef(did_n1)["post_tab"]),
  tab_pre = fmt1(dm_("Tabloid", 0)), tab_post = fmt1(dm_("Tabloid", 1)),
  qual_pre = fmt1(dm_("Quality", 0)), qual_post = fmt1(dm_("Quality", 1)),
  eng_threat     = fmt1(100 * (exp(coef(eng_all)["threatTRUE"]) - 1)),
  eng_opp        = fmt1(100 * (exp(coef(eng_all)["opportunityTRUE"]) - 1)),
  eng_threat_p   = fmtP(pvalue(eng_all)["threatTRUE"]),
  eng_opp_p      = fmtP(pvalue(eng_all)["opportunityTRUE"]),
  wire_pre       = fmt1(wire_tbl$share[wire_tbl$Period == "Pre-launch"]),
  wire_post      = fmt1(wire_tbl$share[wire_tbl$Period == "Post-launch"]),
  web_share      = fmt1(100 * mean(corpus_data$SOURCE_TYPE == "web")),
  named_share    = fmt1(100 * mean(!is.na(corpus_data$outlet))),
  forumhr_share  = fmt1(100 * forum_tab["forum.hr"] / sum(forum_tab)),
  fb_n           = fmtN(sum(corpus_data$SOURCE_TYPE == "facebook")),
  fb_dup         = fmtN(n_distinct(.fbw$id_f)),
  fb_dup_share   = fmt1(100 * n_distinct(.fbw$id_f) / sum(corpus_data$SOURCE_TYPE == "facebook")),
  pre_chatgpt_mentions = fmtN(pre_chatgpt),
  pre_gpt_mentions     = fmtN(pre_gpt),
  pre_gpt_share        = fmt2(100 * pre_gpt / sum(.pre)),
  nofear         = fmt1(robust_tbl$est[robust_tbl$Specification == "Threat without fear/resistance"]),
  nofear_p       = fmt2(robust_tbl$p[robust_tbl$Specification == "Threat without fear/resistance"])
)

# --- Guards: the prose below states these directions; stop if the data disagree ----------
stopifnot(
  its_robust[4, 1] > 0, its_robust[4, 4] < 0.05,         # post-launch slope increase
  its_robust["post", 4] > 0.10,                          # no significant level jump
  coef(did_2way)["post_tab"] < 0,                        # quality > tabloid response
  es_("FEAR_RESISTANCE", late_bins) > es_("FEAR_RESISTANCE", early_bins),
  ate_("SKILLS", "ate") < 0, ate_("SKILLS", "p") < 0.05,
  coef(eng_all)["threatTRUE"] > 0, coef(eng_all)["opportunityTRUE"] < 0,
  placebo_fit["placebo_post", 4] > 0.10,
  mean(composite_monthly$gap[composite_monthly$post == 1]) >
    mean(composite_monthly$gap[composite_monthly$post == 0])
)
```

# Abstract

ChatGPT's November 30, 2022 release made generative artificial intelligence
visible to a mass audience overnight. We treat the launch as an exogenous
shock and trace its effect on Croatian digital media coverage of AI and the
labour market, using `r kn$N` Croatian-language items published between
`r kn$start` and `r kn$end` and drawn from the Determ media-monitoring
database. Coverage did not jump at the launch; it accelerated. Monthly volume
shows no significant level shift in December 2022 but a sustained increase in
its trend (`r kn$its_slope` additional items per month, each month), rising
from `r kn$pre_mean` items a month before the launch to `r kn$post_mean`
after it, and a December 2021 placebo is null. The share of items carrying a
threat frame (job loss, fear, inequality) rose from `r kn$threat_pre`% to
`r kn$threat_post`%, while the opportunity share (job creation,
productivity, transformation) stayed flat; fear-and-resistance framing
continued to grow for more than three years, and skills and reskilling
framing fell and did not recover. Contrary to our prediction, quality
outlets increased threat framing more than tabloids. Threat-framed articles
attract more reader interactions than other articles, consistent with a
demand-side explanation of the shift.

# Introduction

Croatian-language digital coverage of AI and work grew from about
`r kn$pre_mean` items a month before ChatGPT's release to `r kn$post_mean`
a month afterwards, and by `r kn$last_year` it averaged `r kn$last_year_mean`
items a month. Its tone changed with its volume: the share of items
framing AI as a threat to jobs, as a source of fear, or as a driver of
inequality rose from `r kn$threat_pre`% before the launch to
`r kn$threat_post`% after it. Whether generative AI ultimately displaces,
complements, or transforms human work remains an open empirical question
[@acemoglu2018race; @autor2015why; @bessen2020automation]. Workers, firms,
and policymakers must nonetheless act under uncertainty, and the public
information environment that shapes those actions has moved measurably.

Task-level evidence suggests that large language models are exposed to a
wide and disproportionately white-collar share of occupations
[@eloundou2023gpts; @felten2021ai], and field experiments find that
generative AI raises productivity for some workers [@brynjolfsson2023generative].
In a small economy such as Croatia, where firm-level data on AI adoption are
sparse, the main channel through which workers and policymakers learn about
these capabilities is mediated coverage. Which frames that channel
transmits, how quickly, and how persistently is therefore an input to
belief formation and labour-market adjustment.

This paper estimates how the November 30, 2022 ChatGPT release changed
Croatian digital media coverage of AI and the labour market. We treat the
release as an exogenous shock to the salience of generative-AI capabilities
and follow coverage for `r kn$n_pre_months` months before and
`r kn$n_post_months` months after it. The corpus of `r kn$N` items is drawn
from the Determ media-monitoring database through a two-stage filter that
requires both an AI term and a labour-market term. We combine an
interrupted time series for volume, structural-break tests that locate
breaks without imposing the launch date, frame-level event studies, and a
tabloid–quality difference-in-differences.

Four findings stand out. First, the launch changed the *trajectory* of
coverage rather than its level. Monthly volume shows no significant jump in
December 2022 (`r kn$its_level` items, p = `r kn$its_level_p`) but its trend
increases by `r kn$its_slope` items per month, each month, after the launch.
The Bai–Perron procedure dates the first break to `r kn$bp1` (95% interval
`r kn$bp1_lo`–`r kn$bp1_hi`), within three months of the launch, and a
second to `r kn$bp2`; a placebo at December 2021 is null.

Second, the tone of coverage shifted toward threat. The threat share rose
from `r kn$threat_pre`% to `r kn$threat_post`% while the opportunity share
barely moved (`r kn$opp_pre`% to `r kn$opp_post`%). The shift was gradual
rather than abrupt: within 24 months of the launch the threat share is
`r kn$w24` percentage points higher than its trend would predict
(p = `r kn$w24_p`), but over the full sample a linear trend absorbs most of
the change. Fear-and-resistance framing drives the shift, rising by
`r kn$fear_early` points in the first six months and by `r kn$fear_late`
points from December 2024 onward, while skills and reskilling framing fell
by `r fmt1(abs(ate_("SKILLS", "ate")))` points and stayed down.

Third, the prediction that tabloids would amplify threat framing most is
rejected. Quality outlets, which started from a lower threat share,
increased it by more than tabloids did; the difference-in-differences
estimate is `r kn$did_coef` percentage points for tabloids relative to
quality outlets (p = `r kn$did_p` with two-way clustering;
`r kn$did_p_wild` with a wild-cluster bootstrap).

Fourth, readers reward threat framing. Among web articles from the same
outlet in the same month, threat-framed articles receive
`r kn$eng_threat`% more interactions and opportunity-framed articles
`r abs(as.numeric(kn$eng_opp))`% fewer, which is consistent with editors
responding to demand.

The paper contributes to three literatures. For work on automation
expectations [@acemoglu2018race; @autor2022work], it documents the supply
of public information that shapes those expectations in a small European
economy where direct measurement of AI adoption is not available. For work
on media framing of AI [@fasthorvitz2017; @chuan2019framing;
@nguyenhekman2024], most of it descriptive and on English-language media, it
provides event-study evidence around a dated shock, a post-period of almost
four years, and direct evidence on outlet type and reader demand. For work
on the labour-market consequences of generative AI [@eloundou2023gpts;
@felten2021ai; @brynjolfsson2023generative], it supplies a measurable input,
the tone of coverage, that can be linked to vacancy, employment, and
reskilling outcomes.

Section 3 describes the Croatian media market and the conceptual framework.
Section 4 describes the corpus, the frame dictionaries, and the outlet
classification. Section 5 sets out the empirical strategy. Section 6
reports the results, Section 7 the robustness checks, and Sections 8 and 9
discuss and conclude.

# Institutional and Conceptual Background

## The Croatian Media Landscape

Croatia's online news market is served by a small number of national
portals, most of which belong to a handful of domestic and foreign owners.
Styria Media Group, an Austrian company, owns the tabloid *24sata*, which
@perusko2024croatia describes as the best-selling newspaper and one that
attracts large numbers of readers online, as well as *Večernji list* and
*Poslovni dnevnik*. The domestically owned Hanza Media, the print market
leader, publishes *Jutarnji list* and *Slobodna Dalmacija*. United Group
operates Nova TV, whose news portal is *Dnevnik.hr*, and the cable news
channel N1, while the Czech-based CME has owned RTL Hrvatska since 2022
[@perusko2024croatia]. RTL Hrvatska took over the portal *Net.hr* from
Telegram Media Grupa in 2021 [@nethr2021rtl], which continues to publish
*Telegram*. *Index.hr* is independently owned, and *Tportal* is published by
Hrvatski Telekom.

The outlets we analyse by name are listed, with their owners and their
number of items in our corpus, in @tbl-outlets (Section 4.3). They are the
national portals of these groups plus the public broadcaster, two regional
dailies, and specialist technology and business titles. Items from all
other sources enter the aggregate analysis but not the outlet-level
comparisons.

The outlet typology used throughout the paper (Tabloid, Quality, Regional,
Public, Tech, Business) describes editorial model and audience rather than
ownership: an owner group can publish both a tabloid and a quality title, as
Styria does with *24sata* and *Večernji list*. Tabloid outlets (24sata,
Index.hr, Net.hr) prioritise high-volume, attention-driven coverage; quality
outlets (Jutarnji list, Večernji list, Dnevnik.hr, N1, Telegram, Tportal)
run longer analytical pieces. The Tabloid–Quality contrast is the basis for
the difference-in-differences in Section 6.8.

## ChatGPT as a Salience Shock

We treat ChatGPT's November 30, 2022 public release as an unanticipated
shock to the salience of generative-AI capabilities for Croatian editors and
readers. The release was announced and shipped on the same day. Section 5.3
reports the in-corpus evidence: only `r kn$pre_chatgpt_mentions` items in
our corpus mention ChatGPT before the release, and the pre-launch items that
mention OpenAI or GPT concern earlier models.

The treatment date is December 1, 2022, the first month in which every
day is post-release in the monthly aggregation our design uses.

## Conceptual Framework

A short verbal model of editorial choice under attention scarcity yields
three predictions. Editors fill a limited number of article slots to
maximise expected readership, and readers respond more strongly to a vivid
downside than to a measured upside [@soroka2015negativity;
@robertson2023negativity]. A salience shock expands the menu of story angles
and raises the expected return to AI-and-work coverage relative to other
topics competing for the same slots.

Three predictions follow. First, coverage volume rises after the shock,
because the expected return to the topic now exceeds the opportunity cost
of a slot (tested in Sections 6.1–6.2). Second, threat-leaning angles
(displacement, fear, inequality) gain more than opportunity-leaning angles
(job creation, productivity, transformation), because reader negativity
bias makes threat angles more profitable per slot (Sections 6.3–6.6).
Third, outlets whose business model depends most on attention-driven
revenue, tabloids, amplify the threat tilt more than quality outlets that
depend more on subscriptions and reputation [@esser1999tabloidization]
(Section 6.8). The demand-side mechanism behind the second prediction also
implies that threat-framed articles attract more reader engagement, which
we test in Section 6.9.

### Literature review (draft outline for the co-authors)

written.]`

1. **Framing as selection and salience.** @entman1993framing defines
   framing as selecting some aspects of a perceived reality and making them
   more salient; @scheufele1999framing separates media frames (what we
   measure) from audience frames (what we do not);
   @devreese2005framing distinguishes generic from issue-specific frames.
   *Where we fit:* our eight frames are issue-specific frames for AI and
   work, measured as media frames only.
2. **Generic news frames.** @semetkovalkenburg2000 identify conflict,
   human-interest, economic-consequences, responsibility and morality

3. **Media framing of AI.** Long-run trends in US press coverage
   [@fasthorvitz2017]; benefit and risk framing in US newspapers
   [@chuan2019framing]; ethical issues in AI coverage
   [@ouchchy2020headlines]; how news discourse makes sense of automation
   [@nguyenhekman2024]; ChatGPT headlines in UK media [@roeperkins2023].

   @soroka2015negativity, @soroka2019crossnational and
